title: What do you guys think of my very first in game screen shot?
author: codedidit
selftext: Just finished the first tutorial scene wanted to see what everyone thought. Every single asset in this entire scene was made with AI tools.

comments.author: ImpressFederal5086
comments.body: was gonna say i do not like the cheap art style then i saw the sub this was posted in. good luck on your game dev journey, if youre game ends up being fun could be worth finding an artists to make things look less temu

replies.body: this is just a fun project if I was to make it public I’d 100% get a real artist

comments.author: ApprehensiveSkin828
comments.body: Cool. You can add one more depth layer in the caracteres to give more notion of perspective.

replies.author: codedidit
replies.body: This is a great tip. It’s honestly wild how much of a difference things like this make. Thank you!

comments.author: Koden02
comments.body:
Looking at it from a distance it looks fine, but when I look at it at full size I can tell there is graphical inconsistency with the images, lighting inconsistency, and transparency cutout errors with some images.

As a proof of concept it gets the message across of what you want the game to be like but I'd caution you to take a harder look when you finalize the look to make sure that everything looks consistent and not like you were grabbing assets that looked good from different places.  That's going to involve some editing on your part or adjustments to how you generate the assets.

All in all I'd say it's a good step in the right direction but make sure to keep these things in mind going forward if you want success in your project.

looks cool Looks amazing! I'd love to know if you don't mind sharing how you crafted the prompt to get such consistent vector images and color palettes. Also, how did you ensure that a single prompt would recreate the same image consistently in the future?
